# Tameion

> A treasury account for onchain companies that keeps itself solvent: bills
> paid on time inside a limit a smart contract enforces, the owner's passkey
> as the only key that can take money out, every decision provable on chain.

The agent's key can pay payees the owner approved, under a cap, and nothing
else. It cannot add a payee, raise its own limit, or withdraw. Adding a payee
or withdrawing needs the owner's passkey; raising a cap waits a delay the
owner can cancel. Tameion's service holds no key that can take the owner's
money: it prepares calls, the owner's passkey signs them, the chain enforces
them.

## For an AI agent working for the company

- MCP server, the same eighteen tools two ways. Over HTTP, nothing to
  install: `POST /mcp` on this host (Streamable HTTP, MCP 2025-06-18: one
  JSON-RPC message per POST, a JSON reply, 202 for a notification; no SSE
  stream and no session, so GET answers 405), with
  `Authorization: Bearer <agent key>`. Claude Code:

      claude mcp add --transport http --scope project tameion https://<this host>/mcp --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${TAMEION_TOKEN}'

  The single quotes keep `${TAMEION_TOKEN}` a reference: Claude Code reads
  the variable when it connects, and the key never lands in the config file.
  Or over stdio: `tameion-mcp` with `TAMEION_URL` set to this host and, if the
  owner minted one, `TAMEION_TOKEN` set to the agent key. None of the tools
  can sign for the owner. Every tool carries `readOnlyHint` (read and
  `prepare_*` tools only read or compute calldata; `run_pass`, `import_bills`,
  `watch_address` change state, never money). `buy_service` and `pay` spend
  (marked `destructiveHint: true`), and only inside the account's limits.
- Agent keys: the owner's passkey mints a bearer token with scopes `read`,
  `run`, `prepare`, `import`, `buy` and an expiry. Once one exists, the
  account's read / run / prepare / import routes need
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Buying always needs one with `buy`.
- Idempotency: send `Idempotency-Key: <1–255 chars>` on any POST. A retry with
  the same key and body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed:
  true`; the same key with a different body is refused (422); a key still in
  flight answers 409. Keys live 24 hours.
- Every reply is in one envelope (below); HTTP status codes mean what they
  say (400 bad input, 401/403 agent key, 404 no such account, 409, 422, 429,
  502/503 a dependency did not answer).

## Every reply: the envelope (contract 2026-10-18.1)

Every route an agent calls (the MCP tools' routes and every route an agent key
opens) answers in one shape:

    { "ok": true,  "contractVersion": "2026-10-18.1", ...the route's fields }
    { "ok": false, "contractVersion": "2026-10-18.1",
      "error": { "code": "payee_not_approved", "by": "payee", "executed": "no",
                 "audience": "user", "meaning": "...", "nextStep": "...",
                 "retryAfterSecs": 0, "words": "the sentence for a person" } }

- `code`: one of the catalogue below, also served at `GET /api/level1/codes`
  (no key). Read `error.code`; `words` is for the person you work for.
- `by`: who refused — `auth` `input` `mandate` `budget` `payee` `idempotency`
  `chain` `upstream` `service`.
- `executed`: `yes` | `no` | `unknown` — whether the refused action happened.
  After a paid-API purchase's signature reached the seller it is read from
  the chain (`executed(digest)`): `yes` when it settled, `unknown` while the
  seller may still collect or when the read failed. Anything refused before
  sending is `no`.
- `audience`: `user` when a human must act (approve a payee, raise a limit,
  switch mode, sign with the passkey); `agent` when you can act yourself.
- Retry rules: never resend a payment when `executed` is `yes` or `unknown` —
  keep the Idempotency-Key and read the account. Resend once, after
  `retryAfterSecs` (1–60 s), only on `rate_limited` or `idempotency_pending`
  with `executed: "no"`. Every other code needs the change `nextStep` names.
- MCP: a refused tool call is `isError: true`, `content[0].text` is the JSON of
  the `error` object, `structuredContent` is the whole reply;
  `serverInfo.version` is the contract version. Warn once when it changes.
- What changed lately: `recentUpdates` in `GET /api/level1/codes` and in the
  inbox, which also says `paused` (the account is on Watch) and `halt`
  (a read-back mismatch stopped the agent until a human clears it).

The codes:

- Agent key (`auth`): `token_missing` (send one), `token_invalid` (wrong or
  revoked), `token_expired` (owner mints a new one), `token_scope` (the key
  lacks the scope in `scope`), `token_stopped` (the owner stopped this key),
  `needs_owner` (only the owner's passkey or device does this).
- Mandate: `mode_watch` (account paused), `mode_propose` (the agent asks before
  every payment; only Autopilot pays), `agent_lapsed` (renew),
  `account_keyless` (no agent key: the owner pays), `account_not_deployed`
  (not on chain yet), `price_out_of_band` (a price over a quarter above the
  seller's usual waits for the owner), `reservation_not_controlled` (this
  account does not control the reservation; nothing was consumed).
- Budget: `over_per_payment`, `over_24h` (wait for room, `caps.leftNow`),
  `below_floor`, `insufficient_funds`, `over_max_price` (above your maxUsdc).
- Payee: `payee_not_approved` (the ask waits in Needs you), `payee_cooling_off`
  (payable at `payableFrom`), `payee_frozen` (the issuer froze it).
- Idempotency: `idempotency_conflict` (same key, other body),
  `idempotency_pending` (still running), `seller_pending` (an earlier purchase
  from this seller can still be collected), `already_paid`.
- Input: `invalid_body`, `not_found`, `body_too_large`, `state_conflict` (the
  request does not fit the account as it is now: read it first),
  `sig_alg_missing` (the signed body names no `alg`), `sig_alg_unknown` (its
  `alg` is not p256-webauthn, secp256k1-eip712 or ml-dsa-65), `recall_unknown`
  (a cited `evt:<seq>` is not in this account's record).
- Service, chain, upstream: `rate_limited`, `account_busy`,
  `service_unavailable`, `service_paused` (the operator paused it, e.g. the
  demo's relayer is under its floor), `service_error`, `chain_unavailable`,
  `chain_refused` (the contract refused; words say why), `purchase_expired`,
  `upstream_unavailable` (a seller, Circle or a node did not answer as
  expected), `x402_unsupported` (the seller takes no payment this account can
  make).

## What an agent may usefully do

- Read the account: `GET /api/level1/inbox?policy=0x…` — mode, caps, balance,
  what was paid, what waits for the owner: `waiting` (and `waitingCount`) is
  every bill to approve, seller to approve and invoice, the same items the
  account page counts (`needsYou` alone is only the bills). `caps.spent24h`
  and `caps.leftNow` (spent in the trailing 24 hours, and what the contract
  still allows now), `payees` (approved, with `payableFrom` when each one's
  cooling-off ends) and `pending.words` (a change waiting its delay, only what
  is pending) are read from the contract. `run` (every waiting bill as one
  call the owner approves with one tap), runway (days until the first bill
  the policy could not cover) and
  `runway.idleCover` (the part no bill in 90 days needs — report it, never
  suggest where it should earn), `holdingsElsewhere` (USDC in Circle Gateway
  on other chains), `deployed` (false: the address is reserved and the first
  check creates the account there).
- Ask for a check: `POST /api/level1/run {"policy"}` then
  `GET /api/watch/<id>` for progress and the report.
- Tell the agent about a bill: `POST /api/level1/bills` (payee, amount, every N
  days, and the invoice's early-payment terms if any: `discountPercent`,
  `earlyDays`). The owner's passkey still approves the payee. The agent pays
  early for the discount only when every bill in the next 30 days stays
  covered; the Paid row says what it saved.
- Prepare, never sign: `POST /api/level1/prepare-*` returns `{to, data,
  summary}` for the owner's passkey, plus for payees, limits and mode
  `signer` (only the owner's passkey), `applies` (a cut or a revocation at
  once; a raise, Autopilot or a new payee after the account's delay, and the
  owner can cancel until then) and `ownerSees`. Sent with an agent key and a
  `reason`, the request appears on the account page as one row with one tap;
  the page decodes and shows the call in words before the passkey signs.
- Standing orders anyone may trigger on their day: `POST /api/level1/pay-due`.
- Buy a paid API (x402): `POST /api/level1/buy {"policy", "url", "method"?,
  "body"?, "maxUsdc", "reason"}` with a `buy` agent key. The service answers
  the seller's HTTP 402, signs one purchase with the account's agent key and
  sends it by x402's `exact` scheme, ERC-7710 method (the account is the
  delegation manager); the seller's facilitator redeems it on the account,
  which applies the same checks as a bill: approved seller, per-payment cap,
  24-hour limit, floor, Autopilot. A seller nobody approved answers 409 with
  `needsYou` and appears on the account page for one tap; never retry it.
  `inbox.purchases` lists what was bought, with the reason.
- Pay an approved payee: `POST /api/level1/pay {"policy", "payee", "amount",
  "why"}` with a `buy` agent key and `Idempotency-Key: <operation id>` (8 to
  128 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : -; one per payment, the same on a retry). Only on
  Autopilot, only a payee the owner approved and past its cooling-off, inside
  the per-payment cap, the 24-hour limit and the floor: the account's
  contract checks each in the payment's own transaction. The action hash is
  keccak256(policy ‖ operation id), so the chain refuses a second payment
  under the same id; the same id and body answers with the first payment
  (`replayed: true`), a different body is `idempotency_conflict`. `why` is
  written to the account's book beside the payment and anchored with the next
  check. Refusals: `mode_propose`, `mode_watch`, `agent_lapsed`,
  `payee_not_approved`, `payee_cooling_off`, `over_per_payment`, `over_24h`,
  `below_floor`, `insufficient_funds`, `invalid_body`. MCP tool: `pay`.

- A keyless account (`inbox.keyless: true`) has no agent key at all: the
  agent only reads and proposes; tell the owner one tap pays everything
  waiting. Autopilot is refused for it.

- A wallet account (`inbox.delegation` present) is the company's own
  wallet running the policy by EIP-7702. While `delegation.active` is false
  it waits for one transaction only the wallet can send (the authorization
  plus `initialize`, both given in `delegation`); say so, do not retry
  passes. Once active it behaves like any account, at the wallet's address.

- Several owners (`inbox.owners`): an account may need more than one owner's
  passkey for every change (`threshold`). A call one owner approved waits in
  `inbox.approvals` for the others; say how many more are needed. Never
  suggest adding an owner whose pairing code was not checked in person.
- `inbox.exposure`: what the bill wallet holds outside dollars and what a
  30% fall would cost in days of bills. Report it in those words; protection
  needs a trade-only venue key the owner chooses to give.

## Bill a Tameion account (for a vendor, or a vendor's agent)

Send an invoice the PAYEE signed; nothing is paid on receipt. The account's
agent checks it against its history and approved payees and puts it in the
owner's Needs you with what it found; the owner accepts (a recurring invoice
becomes a bill the agent pays inside the caps; a one-off one is paid by the
owner's tap, once, keyed by the invoice's ref) or declines.

- `POST /api/level1/invoice` with the signed body (open: the signature is the
  authentication; twenty an hour per account; 16 KiB):
  `{"version":3,"alg":"secp256k1-eip712","policy","payee","amount":"150000","dueAt","everyDays","discountBps","earlyDays","ref","issuedAt","signature"}`
  — `amount` in USDC minor units (string), `everyDays` 0 = one payment,
  `discountBps` at most 1000 with `earlyDays` shorter than `everyDays`,
  `ref` 32 bytes unique per invoice (a ref already sent is refused).
  201 = received (with the agent's notes); 422 = refused, in words.
- EIP-712: domain `{name: "Tameion Invoice", version: "3", chainId: <the
  account's chain>, verifyingContract: <the account>}`, primary type
  `Invoice(address payee,address policy,uint256 amount,uint64 dueAt,uint32 everyDays,uint16 discountBps,uint16 earlyDays,bytes32 ref,uint64 issuedAt,string from,string domain)`
  (`from` and `domain` may be empty). The signer must be `payee` — the address
  the money goes to. `alg` sits beside the signature, outside the digest; a
  version 3 body without it is `sig_alg_missing`, an unknown one
  `sig_alg_unknown`. Versions 1 and 2 (domain version "1"/"2", no `alg`) are
  accepted until 2026-11-15; the reply carries `deprecated`.
- Post-quantum (FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65): bind the key once,
  `POST /api/level1/key-binding` `{"policy","payee","alg":"ml-dsa-65","pkSha256","boundAt","signature"}`
  signed by the payee's address key (EIP-712 `KeyBinding(address payee,address policy,string alg,bytes32 pkSha256,uint64 boundAt)`,
  domain `{name: "Tameion KeyBinding", version: "1", chainId, verifyingContract}`); then send
  invoices with `"alg":"ml-dsa-65"`, `publicKey` (0x…, 1,952 bytes) and an
  ML-DSA-65 `signature` (3,309 bytes, empty context) over the same digest.
  After binding, that payee's other invoices are refused (`sig_alg_missing`).
- viem: `walletClient.signTypedData({ domain, types: { Invoice: [...] },
  primaryType: "Invoice", message })`; cast: `cast wallet sign --data
  --from-file invoice-typed.json` (the same typed data as JSON). MCP:
  `send_invoice` posts a body you signed; `invoices` lists what waits.

## Live updates, and the agent's identity

- `GET /api/level1/events?policy=<account>` — Server-Sent Events (same auth as the inbox). `hello` on connect;
  `pass` while a check is queued, running (with progress) and when it ends (`paid`, `needsYou`, `anchorTx`);
  `inbox {cause}` after anything changes the account — re-read `/api/level1/inbox`. Ping every 15 s.
- `GET /agents/<account>.json` — the account agent's ERC-8004 registration-v1 card, with the caps read from the
  contract now. `POST /api/level1/identity {policy}` registers the agent itself in the ERC-8004 Identity Registry
  `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e` (Arbitrum Sepolia and Arc testnet); the agent owns that identity.
  Use it to check who you are dealing with before you bill or sell to an account: the card's `wallet` service is the
  only key that pays you, and its `caps` are the most it can pay per call and per day.

## What no agent can do here

- Sign for the owner, add a payee, raise a limit, withdraw, change the key.
- Pay a payee the stablecoin issuer has frozen (Circle's USDC blocklist is
  read from the token on every pass; such a payment is refused, not asked).
- Pay the same bill twice (the contract keeps every settled action hash).

## Price

Watch is free. An account is a flat monthly fee per protected account (free
while on testnet); Tameion takes nothing per payment.

## Reference

- OpenAPI: /api/openapi.json
- Account page: / · receipts and proof: /level1 · read-only report: /watch
- Verify any record on your own machine: download its events from
  `/api/level1/record?policy=…&root=…` (one JSON line per event, in order).
  Recompute: leaf = keccak256(0x00 ‖ the line's `canonical` bytes); with n > 1
  leaves, split at k = the largest power of two below n, node =
  keccak256(0x01 ‖ root(leaves[0:k]) ‖ root(leaves[k:n])); one leaf is its own
  root (RFC 6962 with Keccak-256, not SHA3-256). Compare with `rootOf(agent)`
  on the anchor contract named in `/api/level1/records` (or the anchor
  transaction's input). A match covers the `canonical` bytes; `kind` and
  `note` are carried for people and are not hashed — the note's words sit
  inside `canonical` as an 8-byte big-endian length then UTF-8, so compare
  them before acting on the words.
- Check what you remember before you rely on it:
  `GET /api/level1/recall?policy=…&ids=evt:0,evt:3[&root=…]` (MCP `recall`,
  CLI `tameion recall evt:3`). `evt:N` is the event's `seq` in one record —
  every pass writes its own record from 0 — read in the latest anchored record
  unless you name an earlier root. The service re-hashes each event from its
  `canonical` bytes and folds its path to the root the chain holds (`rootOf`,
  or the anchoring transaction): `verified`, `unverified` (the record changed
  after it was anchored: do not rely on it) or `unknown` (`recall_unknown`: no
  such event; `by: rpc`: no chain to ask, and nothing is verified without it).
  The agent's own sentences cite the events they rest on as `[evt:N]`; a
  sentence citing an event its case was not given is refused and the rule
  decides.
- See who stands behind each record: `GET /api/level1/symbolon?policy=…[&root=…]`.
  Per record (settlement, decision, flow, meter or price check): its `root`,
  `seq`, `leaf`, `kind`, counterparty and amount, and three slots — `agent`,
  `counterparty_slot`, `witness` — each `{alg, keyId, verified}` or null. A
  slot is there only when its check passed in this read: the witness is the
  root's anchoring transaction read back on chain, the counterparty a
  payee-signed invoice the settlement paid; no record carries the agent's own
  signature yet. `counts` says how many records stand behind none, one, two or
  three; `chainReadFailed` lists roots whose anchoring could not be read this
  time (not the same as not witnessed). On an account with agent keys the
  fields and slots need a read key or the owner's device; anyone gets root,
  seq and leaf.
